name: New York
tagline: The World's Cultural Capital — Endless Options at Every Price Point
description: New York City is the ultimate test of a FIRE portfolio — brutally expensive but offering an unmatched density of culture, cuisine, and connection. With world-class healthcare at Mount Sinai and NYU Langone, no car needed thanks to the subway, and a social scene that never sleeps, NYC rewards those with the budget to match its ambitions. The high cost of living means your withdrawal rate works harder, but no other city on earth packs this much life per square block.

quickFacts.visa: No visa required for US citizens
quickFacts.internetSpeed: 300-1000 Mbps fiber available via Verizon Fios and Spectrum
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderately Safe — vastly safer than its reputation; safest large city in America by per-capita crime rates
quickFacts.nearestAirport: John F. Kennedy International (JFK) — 45 min from Manhattan; LaGuardia (LGA) — 30 min; Newark (EWR) — 35 min
quickFacts.climate: Humid continental with cold winters (-3 to 4°C), hot humid summers (24-30°C), and beautiful spring/fall seasons. Four distinct seasons.

housing.description: Compact studio or room-in-share in Washington Heights, Astoria, or Bushwick

dining.description: Dollar slices, halal carts, Chinatown dumplings, bodega breakfasts

healthcare.description: MAGI-managed: NY's Essential Plan runs near-$0 at a managed-low income (≤200% FPL after 1 Jul 2026); nearer the 400%-FPL cliff (~$62,600) a subsidized Silver nets ~$450. $250 = a conservative middle for a genuinely lean, MAGI-managed retiree. Assumes 45–55; older retirees budget more. (NY-specific — see Discrepancy 2)

transportation.description: Unlimited MTA/OMNY monthly cap (~$132); car-free is the norm

entertainment.description: Pay-what-you-wish museums, Central Park, free Prospect Park concerts, rush tickets

1M.lifestyle: A compact studio or a room in a share in Washington Heights, Astoria, or Bushwick is the realistic entry point, because New York's housing floor is the highest in the country and does not collapse for a lean budget. The unlimited MetroCard at roughly $132 a month is the lifeline across all five boroughs, and health cover leans on New York's unusually generous options — the Essential Plan runs near-free at a managed-low income, with a subsidized Silver plan available nearer the cliff. Meals mean dollar slices, dumpling houses, halal carts, and bodega breakfasts, with the Met's pay-what-you-wish policy, Central Park, and free Prospect Park concerts filling the calendar for next to nothing. Every dollar is watched, but the city gives an enormous amount back for free.

housing.description: Nicer studio or small older 1BR in Astoria, Washington Heights, or Sunnyside

dining.description: Out several times a week at solid neighborhood spots

healthcare.description: Silver plan near the subsidy cliff (community-rated, age-flat)

transportation.description: OMNY unlimited plus occasional Lyft and a Citi Bike membership

2M.lifestyle: A nicer studio or a small older one-bedroom in Astoria, Washington Heights, or Sunnyside opens up a real neighborhood with an easy subway ride to the center. Dining out several times a week at solid local spots, a Silver plan near the subsidy cliff, and an unlimited MetroCard with an occasional Lyft and a Citi Bike membership define an enjoyable, unextravagant rhythm. Monthly Broadway shows, museum memberships, and jazz or comedy nights keep the cultural density working in the budget's favor. New York's taxes bite here, but the lifestyle is genuinely good.

housing.description: Spacious 1BR or small 2BR in the West Village, Upper West Side, or Brooklyn Heights

dining.description: Frequent quality dining several nights a week

healthcare.description: Unsubsidized, community-rated (age-flat) broad-network Silver/low-Gold with Mount Sinai / NYU Langone access — the heaviest line, as NY premiums are among the nation's highest (NY benchmark Silver ~$817; broad-network plans run higher; state-avg Silver quoted ~$1,228)

transportation.description: OMNY, Citi Bike, regular Lyft, occasional weekend car service

entertainment.description: Orchestra Broadway, Met Opera, gallery openings, memberships

3M.lifestyle: A spacious one-bedroom or small two-bedroom in the West Village, on the Upper West Side, or in Brooklyn Heights is classic New York living at its best. Dining out lands several nights a week at well-regarded restaurants, and healthcare is a full-price, community-rated plan with access to Mount Sinai and NYU Langone — the heaviest line, since New York's age-flat premiums are among the nation's highest. The subway, Citi Bike, and regular Lyft rides cover the city, with weekend car service to the Hudson Valley or the shore. Orchestra-level Broadway seats, Met Opera evenings, and gallery openings are routine. At $9,000 a month, New York is genuinely affluent, if never quite lavish by Manhattan standards.

housing.description: Luxury doorman 2BR in Tribeca or a brownstone floor-through in the West Village

healthcare.description: Top community-rated plan plus concierge (Sollis Health / One Medical)

transportation.description: Black-car on demand, Citi Bike, occasional Blade, Hamptons Jitney

entertainment.description: Patron memberships (Met/MoMA), MSG box, galas, art-fair previews

domesticHelp.description: Housekeeper several times a week (NYC labor rates)

luxuryExtras.description: Premium fitness, personal stylist, weekend-house share, wardrobe

5M.lifestyle: A luxury doorman two-bedroom in Tribeca or a brownstone floor-through in the West Village, with a housekeeper several times a week, marks upper-affluent New York. Fine dining is a near-daily option, healthcare pairs a top community-rated plan with a Sollis or One Medical concierge membership, and transport means black-car on demand, Citi Bike, and the occasional Blade hop or Jitney to the Hamptons. Patron memberships at the Met and MoMA, a box at the Garden, and art-fair previews are standard, along with a weekend-house share upstate. It is living very well in the priciest neighborhoods on the continent — renting them, not buying.

housing.description: Trophy penthouse in Tribeca or a full-floor residence on Central Park West, white-glove building

dining.description: Daily fine dining plus a part-time private chef

healthcare.description: Elite concierge/longevity care layered over a top community-rated plan

entertainment.description: Board/patron seats, art patronage, major galas

domesticHelp.description: Full staff-for-one household: housekeeper, personal assistant, part-time chef

luxuryExtras.description: Bespoke travel, club memberships, art advisor

10M.lifestyle: A trophy penthouse in Tribeca or a full-floor residence on Central Park West, in a white-glove building with full household staff, sits at the very top of what American city living costs. Dining is daily at the city's best rooms with a part-time private chef for evenings in, healthcare is an elite concierge arrangement layered over a top plan, and a private driver plus a Blade or charter membership erase the friction of the city. Board and patron seats at the major cultural institutions, an art-advisory and philanthropy budget, and bespoke travel are simply part of the year. This is the summit of New York — the most expensive of the US metros by a wide margin — where means translate into an uncapped calendar.
